outline.chapter_title: Chapter 1: Procedural Posture and Factual Background
outline.description: This chapter establishes the narrative foundation of the case, detailing the relationship between the insureds, the premium finance company (APAC), and the insurer (GoAuto). It outlines the specific mechanism of premium financing, the automatic cancellation triggered by non-payment, and the litigation history from state court removal to federal summary judgment.
subtopics: The Tripartite Relationship: Insureds, APAC (Finance Company), and GoAuto (Insurer)
The Power of Attorney Mechanism: How APAC is authorized to cancel policies
The Trigger Event: Non-payment leading to automated cancellation procedures
Litigation History: State court filing, removal to federal court, and grounds for dismissal
Procedural Status at Appeal: Summary Judgment ruling in favor of GoAuto

outline.chapter_title: Chapter 2: Governing Law and Statutory Requirements for Cancellation
outline.description: This chapter analyzes the specific provisions of Louisiana Revised Statutes § 9:3550(G)(3) that regulate insurance cancellations by premium finance companies. It breaks down the mandatory steps required for a valid cancellation request and explains the judicial doctrine of 'strict adherence' established by Louisiana precedent.
subtopics: Mandatory Elements of a Valid Cancellation Request (Power of Attorney, Default Status, Notice to Insured, Notice to Interested Parties)
The Doctrine of Strict Adherence: Why defects render cancellation ineffective
